files.change: In validateExpense, extend the MAX_INT8 per-field bound on split inputs (currently splitType==='exact' only) to also apply when splitType==='shares', refusing with the identical sentence 'That amount is too large to record.' keyed at input.<memberId> via the existing ??= so a parse refusal keeps precedence; and correct the comment above it that claims a share count is a weight needing no bound — percentages truly need none (any oversized input fails the sum==10000 check before the insert), but a shares count is stored verbatim in expense_split_input.input_value (int8).

qa_script: Seed, sign in, and open a group with at least two members.

Record an expense with split type shares and 99999999999999999999999 in one member's shares field; expect the per-field sentence 'That amount is too large to record.' and no new expense in the list or feed.
Record the same expense with small share counts; expect success and one expense.added feed entry.
Reopen the expense, switch nothing, save; expect the stored shares to round-trip unchanged.
risks: The guard sits in validateExpense, which both createExpense and updateExpense share, so a typo in the condition would break both paths; the new cases plus the existing amount/payer/exact bound suite pin it.
No forbidden paths are touched and the app sends data to no new host.
work_order.root_cause: validateExpense bounds the amount, payer parts and exact inputs against MAX_INT8 but leaves shares inputs unbounded; parseDecimal builds an arbitrary-size BigInt, so a share count above 9223372036854775807 passes validation and is written verbatim to expense_split_input.input_value (int8), where Postgres raises out-of-range and the action answers 500 instead of a field sentence. The second review finding (tests/lib/money.test.ts listed in neither files[] nor tests[]) still holds as written but is benign unit coverage for in-scope helpers and needs no code change, so it is dropped from this plan.

cases: Refuses a shares input above the int8 maximum (e.g. '99999999999999999999999') beside that member's field with 'That amount is too large to record.', writing no expense, payer, share, input or activity rows (mirrors the existing exact-input case).
Accepts a shares input of exactly the int8 maximum (9223372036854775807) and stores it exactly in expense_split_input (the bound is above-max, not at-max).

work_order.understanding: Issue #33 carries two review findings from PR #29: (1) a shares-split input has no int8 bound, so a count above 9223372036854775807 passes validation and explodes at the insert with a 500 instead of a field sentence — still true in src/app/actions/expenses.ts:304, which bounds only exact inputs; (2) tests/lib/money.test.ts gained benign unit coverage outside the work-order lists — still true, and needs no code change. This plan fixes (1) with the mirrored bound the review prescribes and drops (2) as recorded-but-benign.
